correctness.rationale: The order-six Fourier indicator is exact. A support-by-support Weil bound gives 216N(q)>=q-108-325sqrt(q), strictly positive above the precise finite threshold 105841. The standalone exact checker enumerates every relevant prime and extension below the threshold (5037 primes; 77 proper powers), certifies all extension polynomial irreducibility and multiplicative generators, checks all 35 negative fields exhaustively, and supplies witnesses for every other small field. Computation is finite and is only combined with the independent analytic tail; the main limit is trust in the inspectable exact checker.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 Cohen article gives the NS3 PAIR classification, and its explicit triple question establishes natural motivation but not this sharper complete NS3 triple classification. Lehmer et al. 1962 classify weaker cubic-residue triples at primes; Gun et al. 2007 give sufficiently large-prime NSNP strings under broader hypotheses. Multiple published-finding corpus and literature searches gave no equivalent 35-field classification. Partial older six-power-residue overlap (Buell-Hudson 1986) is a real unresolved risk, not a proven noncoverage.
residual_risks: Uninspected 1986 Buell--Hudson article may include or imply some results on consecutive sixth powers; q=7 mod12 has an exact negation equivalence.
Unindexed historical cyclotomic number tables could implicitly compute some or all exceptional orders.
Exact finite computation relies on inspecting and running standalone arithmetic code; no independent audit or external formal verification.

value.rationale: Classifies all fields of order 1 mod 6 in which a natural canonical multiplicative coset contains three consecutive additive translates, an explicitly motivated strengthening of recent NS3-pair work and its triple question. It is a complete 35-exception all-prime-power theorem with uniform analytic cutoff and exhaustive certificates for the finite region. It does not merely tabulate an arbitrary range or rephrase a known bound.
